human_advice.authority_boundary: Acknowledges advice that changed public files in this repository. It does not say that the person reviewed, checked or endorsed any mathematics, and it does not make them an author.

entries.title: Explaining the calculation behind the number line
entries.told: Jasmine Otto pointed out that the dots on the number line did not make the remainder calculation clear in an early #257 preview.
entries.changed: Her feedback helped focus the new lesson on multiplying the fraction, subtracting the whole part, and connecting the remainder to the number line.
The communication rules now require an inspectable comparison and evidence for a claimed advantage, while keeping an invitation to look distinct from a completed review.
entries.title: Showing an inspectable comparison
entries.told: A researcher advised showing a clear advantage over existing systems when asking people to use the work.

entries.changed: The explanation now distinguishes persistent records for inspection and continuation from a model’s problem-solving capability; the distinction is also published in the credit policy.
entries.title: Clarifying the role of persistent research records
entries.told: A researcher challenged the framing of the system as an external improvement to rapidly advancing models.

entries.changed: All sixteen problem papers were rewritten for a first-time reader, naming standard tools and saying how restrictive each hypothesis is, and the public writing rules now require it.
entries.title: Writing for a first-time reader
entries.told: A mathematician said the #243 note used names that meant nothing on a first or second reading, defined notation it used once, and never said how restrictive its main hypothesis was.

entries.changed: A literature review was run for each of the eight problems, and each paper now credits its sources at the point where they are used.
entries.title: Showing where methods and ideas come from
entries.told: A mathematician said the trouble with AI-assisted mathematics is that it rarely shows where its methods and ideas come from.

entries.changed: The #249 paper now opens with the exact rank and basis, compares the result with work of Allouche and Shallit, Coons and Martin, and links a minimal Lean entry; the irrationality question stays open.
entries.title: Leading the #249 paper with its exact theorem
entries.told: A mathematician advised leading the #249 paper with its exact finite-level theorem, explaining the mechanism behind it, and comparing it precisely with the existing literature on regular sequences.

entries.changed: formalization.yaml now lists the selected results this way, and Comparator checks them against separately written statements, including an altered statement that must be rejected.
entries.title: Listing each checked result, with a cheap way to check it
entries.told: A mathematician advised listing each selected result with its exact statement, proof source, novelty status, axioms and limits, and giving reviewers a cheap way to check the statements themselves.

entries.changed: That connection was removed from future correspondence unless new evidence supports it; the published credit policy records the same rule for correcting scope.
entries.title: Removing an unsupported specialist connection
entries.told: A mathematician saw no connection between their specialist methods and the question presented to them.

entries.changed: The comparison was carried out: a source note and a Lean module recording where the two methods part are public, and the #1049 record cites the paper where they meet.
entries.title: Earlier work on the #1049 Lambert value
entries.told: A mathematician suggested comparing the #1049 construction with an earlier irrationality paper.

entries.changed: The correspondence rules now require one concrete object, its purpose, a narrow request and a clear reading or time cost; those rules are also published in the credit policy.
entries.title: Explaining the purpose of the work
entries.told: A reader could not identify the system’s goal, the object being shown, or why its interface was useful.

human_advice.naming_policy: Every entry starts with the name withheld. A name appears only after that person confirms the public name they want, and an entry stays anonymous if they ask. Private messages stay outside this repository.

source_evidence.excerpt:
- `research/continuation_learning.py` and its deterministic demo/tests are a
  maintained, modified adaptation of the witness-preserving rational-linear
  learner and selector in Zenith progress return 02, not a copy of that return's
  research results. Source archive:
  `ZENITH_PROGRESS_RETURN_02-selecting-questions-that-pay.zip`, SHA-256
  `5fe705df566a41de013242664f62a23e63b7d0e8eebf796856ebc85b4f148926`.
  The return retains its Apache-2.0 `LICENSE` and attribution in `NOTICE.md`.
- `research/direct_investigation.py` adapts the bounded direct-query interface
  proposed in Zenith progress return 17; the live implementation adds strict
  delivery, accounting and replay integration. Source archive:
  `ZENITH_PROGRESS_RETURN_17-using-the-models-capabilities-properly.zip`,
  SHA-256 `2c7ce604160b47b91b9e031273fb35e180022682e4ceb2665270ca96bccb899a`.
  The return retains its Apache-2.0 `LICENSE` and `ATTRIBUTION.md`.
- `research/native_conformance_tasks.py::authored_fixed_queries` adapts the
  standards-informed UTF-8 boundary probe pack from Zenith progress return 16
  as an authored fixed rival. It is not an acquired investigation policy.
  Source archive:
  `ZENITH_PROGRESS_RETURN_16-strong-rivals-and-independent-challenges.zip`,
  SHA-256 `2f4d83895fbe8f925d2d4853317fc9b08f0cd0bfccb2106aac0f87b1dd4993ee`.
